Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) and local Provincial Mercantile Registries.

Governing statute

Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio), Articles 20-22 (incorporation), 58-60 (registered office), 209-210 (board of directors), 214-215 (appointment of officers).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (Deed of Incorporation) executed before a Spanish Notary.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 40 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Minimum capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation. Capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name; the deposit certificate is attached to the deed. No escrow account is required beyond the initial deposit.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (Servicio de Extinción de Incendios) confirming compliance with NFPA and Spanish regulations (CTE). Structural load inspection by a certified engineer for the building. Occupational health and safety clearance from the Instituto Nacional de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (INSST) and regional labor authority, including workplace risk assessment and emergency plans.

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation. Capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name; the deposit certificate is attached to the deed. No escrow account is required beyond the initial deposit.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Madrid; electronic filing and certification portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); customs and excise directorate within AEAT (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) manages export declarations and EORI issuance.

E-government filing portal

For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) engaged in medical-device manufacturing and export: Step 1 – before notarized incorporation, obtain a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via AEAT form 036 filed by the incorporators; Step 2 – after execution of the public deed and mandatory registration in the Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry), file the definitive CIF/NIF application with form 036 within one month; the definitive NIF for a capital company follows the pattern B-8 digits-control; Step 3 – complete the mandatory Censo de Empresarios (census of business operators) on the same form 036, simultaneously making the IVA registration and the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) enrolment for ISIC 3250 manufacturing activity before beginning operations; Step 4 – apply for an EORI number (ES+9 digits) from AEAT customs for export declarations; Step 5 – non-resident shareholders are permitted without restriction, but a Spanish tax representative may be required where the entity or non-EU owners trigger asset-holding rules; foreign entities not resident in Spain require a foreign-operator NIF (letter N prefix) to perform taxable transactions. The entire procedure is completed electronically with AEAT digital certificates, with a standard issuance time of 5-10 business days after the commercial-registry filing.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; the SL is a Spanish tax-resident entity, taxed on worldwide income under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) at the general rate of 25%; a reduced 20% rate applies to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable income of qualifying micro-enterprises with net turnover below EUR 1,000,000 (Ley 7/2024 reform), and a 15% rate may apply to certified innovative startups under Ley 28/2022; profits distributed to non-resident shareholders face withholding tax of 19% (20% from 1 January 2025); no flow-through or partnership-style pass-through treatment is available for an SL. — For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) engaged in medical-device manufacturing and export: Step 1 – before notarized incorporation, obtain a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via AEAT form 036 filed by the incorporators; Step 2 – after execution of the public deed and mandatory registration in the Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry), file the definitive CIF/NIF application with form 036 within one month; the definitive NIF for a capital company follows the pattern B-8 digits-control; Step 3 – complete the mandatory Censo de Empresarios (census of business operators) on the same form 036, simultaneously making the IVA registration and the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) enrolment for ISIC 3250 manufacturing activity before beginning operations; Step 4 – apply for an EORI number (ES+9 digits) from AEAT customs for export declarations; Step 5 – non-resident shareholders are permitted without restriction, but a Spanish tax representative may be required where the entity or non-EU owners trigger asset-holding rules; foreign entities not resident in Spain require a foreign-operator NIF (letter N prefix) to perform taxable transactions. The entire procedure is completed electronically with AEAT digital certificates, with a standard issuance time of 5-10 business days after the commercial-registry filing.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; the SL is a Spanish tax-resident entity, taxed on worldwide income under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) at the general rate of 25%; a reduced 20% rate applies to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable income of qualifying micro-enterprises with net turnover below EUR 1,000,000 (Ley 7/2024 reform), and a 15% rate may apply to certified innovative startups under Ley 28/2022; profits distributed to non-resident shareholders face withholding tax of 19% (20% from 1 January 2025); no flow-through or partnership-style pass-through treatment is available for an SL.

Available election forms

Spain has no check-the-box equivalent; however, elections and option regimes available to an SL include: (1) option to form a consolidated tax group (régimen de consolidación fiscal) with direct or indirect 70% or greater Spanish subsidiaries, subject to prior AEAT authorization (art. 100 Ley 27/2014); (2) election for micro-enterprise reduced rates where the EUR 1M turnover and related-party conditions are met; (3) startup certification election under Ley 28/2022 for the 15% rate; (4) option to apply the territorial/offset credit method for foreign-source income with electable exemptions for qualifying foreign branch profits; (5) VAT group election (grupo de IVA) for entities with at least 50% control; (6) hybrid mismatch elections limited to the ATAD anti-hybrid mechanism – Spain does not permit unilateral entity-classification check-the-box, so hybrid structures must follow the mandatory ATAD 1 and 2 overriding rules.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No de-minimis turnover threshold for Spanish-resident manufacturers: an SL must register for IVA (alta censal) before making any taxable supply; registration is compulsory regardless of revenue level under the general régime. For non-resident EU distance sellers and electronic-services providers the cross-border B2C Union scheme threshold is EUR 10,000. The simplified IVA régime and recargo de equivalencia are not available for ISIC 3250 manufacturing activities; the SL is placed in the general IVA régime with quarterly (modelo 303) or monthly (for large taxpayers and SII filers) returns and annual model 390.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods to third countries (outside the European Union) are zero-rated as exempt with credit of input VAT under art. 21.1 of Ley 37/1992, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter proves the exit; the SL must hold export status, use a valid EORI, and file the electronic DUA. Intra-EU dispatches of the ultrasound consoles to other Member States are exempt with credit under art. 25 of Ley 37/1992 subject to the customer's VIES number and the recapitulative Intrastat/VIES declarations. Related offshore services directly linked to exported goods, such as installation, calibration, training, and after-sales tele-diagnostics of the colour Doppler ultrasound console, are also zero-rated under the territoriality rules of arts. 69-70 Ley 37/1992 where performed for a non-EU recipient. The exported medical device must be lawfully placed on the market under EU MDR 2017/745 and the SL must retain the EC Declaration of Conformity to support the commercial validity of the export.

  • Customs export declaration – DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) filed electronically via the AEAT customs system, including the EORI of the exporter and the HS classification of the phased-array ultrasound console.
  • Transport evidence evidencing EU exit within 90 days – Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or CMR (road), with terminal departure stamps or electronic exit confirmation.
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/MT950 confirmation evidencing full and timely collection of the export proceeds from the non-EU buyer.
  • Commercial invoice, packing list, proforma or sales contract, Incoterms clause, and insurance certificate, referenced to the DUA export number.
  • Technical-legal documentary package: EC Declaration of Conformity under EU MDR 2017/745, Notified Body certificate, and serial-number provenance for the medical imaging console.

Dual regime: (1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) applies mandatorily to taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000, to VAT-group members, and to entities in the deferred-import régime; SII filers transmit invoice record data (issued, received, and capital goods) to AEAT via XML web-services API within 4 calendar days for issued invoices and 8 calendar days for received invoices, with no issuance-stamping requirement; (2) Verifactu (Real Decreto 1007/2023, applicable from 1 July 2025) obliges all B2B invoicing software to guarantee invoice integrity, traceability, and accessibility through a hash-chaining algorithm or QR code, and to transmit entries to AEAT on demand; (3) mandatory structured B2B electronic invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece remains pending final implementation order, with expected phasing for taxpayers above EUR 8,000,000 turnover and afterwards for all businesses; the SL manufacturing medical devices must therefore deploy Verifactu-compliant billing software, maintain the Libro Mayor of invoices, and be prepared for SII obligations once turnover thresholds are exceeded.

AEAT applies a 4-year statute of limitations to VAT assessments. Where an export zero-rating claim fails the documentary or exit-evidence test, AEAT regularizes the sale, charging the 21% VAT omitted, late interest (3.75% for 2025, updated quarterly), and an infringement penalty of 50%-150% of the tax amount for grave offences under arts. 191 and 194 of the Ley General Tributaria (Ley 58/2003); failing to maintain normal books or Verifactu invoicing records triggers fixed penalties of EUR 150-EUR 6,000 per invoice (art. 201 LGT). Wrongfully obtained export VAT refunds are retrospectively clawed back with accrued interest. If the defrauded VAT or CIT amount exceeds EUR 120,000, the action constitutes criminal tax fraud under art. 305 Código Penal, exposing the directors to imprisonment of 1-6 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of state subsidies; AEAT also applies targeted audit programmes on high-risk export chains in the medical-technology sector, including cross-border exchange of information with customs administrations at the port of exit.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and is within the euro area single currency and Single Euro Payments Area. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted for legitimate trade, services, dividends, interest, royalties, salary payments, and other ordinary commercial transactions. Capital-account transactions are generally liberalised, including foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, acquisitions, repatriation of capital, and liquidation proceeds. Spanish banks may nevertheless require documentary evidence of the legal and commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, tax residence, source of funds, and underlying transaction under anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, payment-services, and tax-reporting rules. Profit remittances normally require distributable profits, approved annual accounts, proper corporate approvals, applicable withholding-tax analysis, and evidence that the payment is not an unlawful return of capital or disguised distribution. Payments to non-residents may trigger Spanish withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under Spanish domestic law, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in Spain, an applicable tax treaty, or other applicable exemption. Banks may delay or reject payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, high-risk counterparties, unusual trade flows, inadequate medical-device documentation, or unexplained third-party payments.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Banco de España, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's commercial discretion, subject to bank terms, accounting requirements, tax rules, sanctions screening, and accurate external-trade and balance-of-payments reporting where applicable. Banks may request invoices, customs evidence, transport documents, customer identification, and proof of delivery. Intrastat obligations may apply to qualifying intra-EU movements, while customs declarations and export evidence apply to qualifying extra-EU exports. Cross-border transactions may be reportable through Banco de España external-sector information systems when applicable thresholds, reporting requests, statistical requirements, or regulated-sector rules apply; the precise reporting obligation should be confirmed with the bank and current Banco de España instructions.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España, acting within the framework of the European Central Bank and the European System of Central Banks; foreign-exchange and external-reporting matters are also subject to the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and applicable European Union law.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium for payment operations and low to medium as a replacement for a principal Spanish commercial-bank relationship. A European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may passport services into Spain, subject to its home-state authorisation, passport notification, AML controls, safeguarding regime, and product permissions. An electronic-money institution cannot accept deposits as a bank and normally provides safeguarded payment balances rather than deposit-guaranteed bank deposits. Offshore digital EMIs without relevant European Economic Area authorisation, passporting, or an appropriate Spanish establishment should not be used for regulated payment services to or from the Spanish company. Fintech accounts may be unsuitable for capital contributions, bank guarantees, commercial letters of credit, cash pooling, high-value medical-device trade, or transactions requiring detailed bank documentary review. The company should retain a Spanish or European Economic Area credit institution for core treasury, reserve liquidity, trade finance, and contingency banking.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Unclear or multilayered ownership, failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, or mismatch between the shareholder register, corporate documents, and bank declarations.

Root cause: Unclear or multilayered ownership, failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, or mismatch between the shareholder register, corporate documents, and bank declarations.

Defense evidence: Current Spanish Commercial Registry extract; deed of incorporation and amendments; shareholder register or equivalent ownership evidence; ownership chart to natural persons; passports and address evidence for directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners; beneficial-owner declaration; tax identification numbers; and notarised, apostilled, legalised, or certified translations where requested.
Non-resident ownership or directors with no established Spanish operating footprint.

Root cause: Non-resident ownership or directors with no established Spanish operating footprint.

Defense evidence: Business plan; Spanish registered-office evidence; lease or service agreement; expected transaction and country matrix; customer and supplier profile; employment and logistics plan; Spanish tax registrations; licences or registrations relevant to medical-device activities; group structure; intercompany agreements; and explanation of the commercial rationale for Spanish incorporation.
Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or large initial transfers.

Root cause: Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or large initial transfers.

Defense evidence: Board and shareholder resolutions; subscription or capital-increase documents; shareholder-loan agreement where applicable; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; bank statements; tax returns or financial statements; sale or financing documents supporting wealth origin; payment trail from the beneficial owner or documented group treasury account; and written confirmation of the intended use of funds.
Expected export activity involving Latin America, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, intermediaries, or third-party payments.

Root cause: Expected export activity involving Latin America, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, intermediaries, or third-party payments.

Defense evidence: Customer due-diligence files; distributor and agent agreements; end-user certificates; sanctions screening records; export-control classification; customs documentation; commercial invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading or airway bills; insurance documents; proof of delivery; beneficial-owner information for counterparties; anti-bribery procedures; and documented approval of any third-party payment.
Medical-device manufacturing or export activity without a coherent regulatory and product-compliance file.

Root cause: Medical-device manufacturing or export activity without a coherent regulatory and product-compliance file.

Defense evidence: Applicable European Union Medical Device Regulation analysis; manufacturer, importer, or distributor role assessment; CE-marking and conformity documentation where applicable; registration and economic-operator information; quality-management certificates; product catalogue; device classification; authorised-representative arrangements where relevant; customs classification; product-liability insurance; and evidence that the proposed activity matches the company's registered business purpose.
Expected transaction volumes, currencies, or counterparties inconsistent with the declared business model.

Root cause: Expected transaction volumes, currencies, or counterparties inconsistent with the declared business model.

Defense evidence: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast; monthly transaction-volume and value estimates; currency exposure schedule; projected gross margins; principal customer and supplier list; sample invoices and contracts; treasury policy; reconciliation controls; segregation-of-duties matrix; and escalation procedures for unusual transactions.
PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, corruption, tax-evasion, or high-risk-country exposure involving a director, owner, customer, supplier, or intermediary.

Root cause: PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, corruption, tax-evasion, or high-risk-country exposure involving a director, owner, customer, supplier, or intermediary.

Defense evidence: Completed enhanced-due-diligence questionnaire; independent identity and ownership verification; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; sanctions and adverse-media search records; risk assessment; senior-management approval; anti-corruption representations; contractual compliance clauses; payment restrictions; and ongoing monitoring plan.
Use of cash, personal accounts, anonymous payment providers, cryptoasset platforms, or unrelated third-party accounts.

Root cause: Use of cash, personal accounts, anonymous payment providers, cryptoasset platforms, or unrelated third-party accounts.

Defense evidence: Written prohibition or tightly controlled exception policy; rationale for any exceptional payment; full counterparty verification; bank-origin payment evidence; reconciliations; invoices and contracts; tax treatment; compliance approval; and evidence that all operating receipts and disbursements are routed through accounts held in the company's legal name.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity contributions, share-premium payments, and shareholder loans from an account held in the legal name of the documented shareholder or group treasury entity to the Spanish SL's account at an EU credit institution. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA currencies. State an accurate payment narrative such as 'share capital contribution', 'share premium contribution', or 'shareholder loan under agreement', and do not use generic descriptions that obscure the legal purpose. Maintain the shareholder or board resolution, subscription or loan agreement, bank confirmation, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner evidence, and accounting entry. For a capital increase, coordinate the notarial deed, payment evidence, Commercial Registry filing, and any required tax or corporate records. Do not route capital through personal accounts or unrelated third parties. The receiving bank may request evidence of the commercial purpose, source of funds, tax residence, group relationship, and ultimate beneficiary before crediting or releasing the funds.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA payments, with complete originator, beneficiary, address, bank identifier, invoice reference, currency, and purpose information. For larger or higher-risk medical-device purchases and exports, use documentary Commercial Letters of Credit subject to UCP 600, bank-confirmed letters of credit where commercially justified, documentary collections under URC 522, or open-account terms supported by credit insurance and counterparty controls. A bank may request the commercial invoice, purchase order, sales contract, customs classification, export or import declaration, transport document, insurance certificate, certificate of origin, end-user certificate, and evidence of delivery. Payment release must be consistent with sanctions, export-control, AML, tax, customs, and anti-bribery requirements. Reconcile all wires and trade-finance drawings to the general ledger, invoice, customs file, and approved treasury forecast.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for identified commercial exposures, subject to bank credit limits, documented hedging purpose, confirmation terms, valuation, collateral or margin requirements, and applicable EU financial-market rules.Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or where settlement is contractually cash-settled, subject to the bank's product approval, legal enforceability, sanctions review, suitability or appropriateness assessment, and documented underlying exposure.Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for recurring or material currency and funding exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, EMIR obligations where applicable, collateral and valuation controls, counterparty limits, and board-approved treasury policy.Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options or option collars may be used only where the company understands premium, exercise, liquidity, accounting, and potential contingent-obligation consequences and the bank has completed the required appropriateness and documentation process.Hedging should be limited to genuine forecast, committed, or balance-sheet exposures; speculative trading, excessive leverage, unapproved rolling positions, and hedges that cannot be reconciled to an underlying exposure should be prohibited by treasury policy.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium for payment operations and low to medium as a replacement for a principal Spanish commercial-bank relationship. A European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may passport services into Spain, subject to its home-state authorisation, passport notification, AML controls, safeguarding regime, and product permissions. An electronic-money institution cannot accept deposits as a bank and normally provides safeguarded payment balances rather than deposit-guaranteed bank deposits. Offshore digital EMIs without relevant European Economic Area authorisation, passporting, or an appropriate Spanish establishment should not be used for regulated payment services to or from the Spanish company. Fintech accounts may be unsuitable for capital contributions, bank guarantees, commercial letters of credit, cash pooling, high-value medical-device trade, or transactions requiring detailed bank documentary review. The company should retain a Spanish or European Economic Area credit institution for core treasury, reserve liquidity, trade finance, and contingency banking.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

25%

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the fiscal year-end (i.e., for a 31-Dec year-end, by 25 July; for other year-ends, by the 25th of the month following the six-month post-close period)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 (Identificación/NIF) Spanish NIF, company name, registered address, principal activity code (CNAE) and balance sheet date of the SL. This box reports only the resident SL identity; non-resident shareholders are reported separately in the ownership annex. Late-filing surcharge: 5% of the assessed amount if filed before any tax-authority demand; 10% within 15 days after formal demand, 15% within 30 days, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Non-filing may trigger administrative assessment and penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax.
Box 10 (Resultado contable) Book profit or loss for the fiscal period after depreciation, amortisation and provisions in the statutory annual accounts. No non-resident filing obligation; the SL is the standalone taxpayer. Late-filing surcharge: 5% of the assessed amount if filed before any tax-authority demand; 10% within 15 days after formal demand, 15% within 30 days, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Non-filing may trigger administrative assessment and penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax.
Box 15 (Base imponible) Taxable base after permanent and temporary adjustments, including the offset of prior tax losses and tax-free balancing entries. Base is computed from Spanish CIT rules; the foreign shareholder cannot claim foreign losses in this box. Late-filing surcharge: 5% of the assessed amount if filed before any tax-authority demand; 10% within 15 days after formal demand, 15% within 30 days, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Non-filing may trigger administrative assessment and penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax.
Box 25 (Cuota íntegra) Gross corporate tax liability at the applicable tax rate before deductions, exemptions and double-tax relief. Reduced tax rates or DTA-credits attributed to a shareholder are not applied at this box. Late-filing surcharge: 5% of the assessed amount if filed before any tax-authority demand; 10% within 15 days after formal demand, 15% within 30 days, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Non-filing may trigger administrative assessment and penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax.
Box 155 (Cuota diferencial) Final payable or refundable amount after deductions (e.g., R&D credits, double-tax credit) and withholding credits/prepayments. If the result is refundable, the SL may claim refund; a foreign parent has no direct set-off right in Model 200. Late-filing surcharge: 5% of the assessed amount if filed before any tax-authority demand; 10% within 15 days after formal demand, 15% within 30 days, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Non-filing may trigger administrative assessment and penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Full Local File and Master File are mandatory once annual turnover exceeds EUR 10 million. In all cases, if the aggregate value of related-party transactions with one counterparty or per single operation exceeds EUR 250,000, Form 232 (declaración informativa de operaciones vinculadas) must be filed. Small taxpayers under the EUR 10 million threshold may use a simplified TP summary if requested by AEAT.

Economic substance scope: No offshore ESR regime is applied as such in Spain; however art. 15 Law 27/2014 gives precedence to economic reality and prohibits result-neutral legal forms. A color-doppler device distribution SL with no personnel, premises, risks and substantive commercial activity can be recharacterised as a mere treasury/artificial entity; DAC-6 scheme notification and the doctrine of lifting the corporate veil will be applied.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion / intentional misdeclaration (delito fiscal)

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax due (art. 191 LGT), plus late-payment interest. In criminal cases, art. 305 Código Penal imposes imprisonment of 1 to 4 years, a fine equal to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of public aid and licences.

Director personal liability: Directors or beneficial owners who caused or acquiesced in the fraud are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties under art. 42 LGT. If criminal liability attaches, the court may order pretrial imprisonment, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and piercing of the corporate veil to satisfy restitution.
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Controlled Transaction Misreporting

Statutory sanction: Arm's-length adjustment increasing taxable income and other tax corrections; penalties for non-filing/incomplete Form 232 (up to EUR 10,000 per omission) plus a 15% penalty over the value of the disputed related-party transaction if false said data; interest from the date the return was due.

Director personal liability: Administrators who deliberately omitted or manipulated the TP documentation are jointly and severally liable for the assessments and penalties attributable to their malicious fault. Continued intentional mispricing may be treated as fraud, resulting in criminal prosecution for the legal representative, disqualification from holding managing roles, and preventive travel restrictions.
Shell / Artificial Structure, Money Laundering and AML disregard

Statutory sanction: Tax recharacterisation, loss of taxation benefits; under art. 301 Código Penal money-laundering sanctions include imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years, fines up to three times the laundered value, and forfeiture of profits. The Bank of Spain may suspend license/trading activity and the AEAT can cancel the SL's NIF for lack of economic existence.

Director personal liability: Nominee directors and beneficial owners face liability for all hidden economic assets, joint civil liability for the corporate debt, criminal imprisonment for money laundering if they knowingly control the assets, orders to travel-banned presence for oral cross-examination, and enforcement of personal assets for the tax and criminal financial obligations.
